key_insight: An extended forked PINN separates simulation and control gradients, making joint learning stable for non-Markovian open quantum dynamics.
engineering_relevance: This enables end-to-end differentiable quantum simulation and control, improving state-preparation performance with smoother, more experimentally feasible pulses.
method: Adds a dedicated control branch to the existing FPINN architecture
Uses selective gradient flow to decouple conflicting optimization objectives at the gradient level
Trains jointly on coupled open-system dynamics without sacrificing simulation or control quality
evidence_signal: On a two-qubit Heisenberg XXX model, the method reproduces non-Markovian effects and outperforms gradient ascent pulse engineering, chopped random basis, and standard PINNs in state-preparation fidelity.
watch_item: Results are demonstrated on a specific two-qubit benchmark, so scalability and performance on larger or more realistic hardware remains to be validated.
paper_title: Forked Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Non-Markovian Open Quantum Dynamics and Control
